title: Compose portable command worker deployment
description: Compose and validate the Plexus-owned command-service companion deployment from the existing portable lifecycle, Celery delivery adapter, durable state, container artifact, and always-on worker constructs. Keep it outside the Amplify stacks and the legacy mixed infrastructure application. Require a complete dashboard submission, execution, projection, and deployment proof before it is eligible for main.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Implemented the reusable always-on Fargate deployment stack in plexus.infrastructure.command_service.worker_stack. It composes the durable state stack with a consumer-owned immutable image, private networking, explicit egress, narrow DynamoDB/SQS permissions, Secrets Manager injection, deployment rollback, logs, and a running-task alarm. It contains no consumer or legacy command-runtime behavior. Local validation passed: python -m pytest infrastructure/tests/unit/test_command_service_state_stack.py infrastructure/tests/unit/test_command_service_worker_stack.py -q; ruff check plexus/infrastructure/command_service infrastructure/tests/unit/test_command_service_state_stack.py infrastructure/tests/unit/test_command_service_worker_stack.py; black --check plexus/infrastructure/command_service infrastructure/tests/unit/test_command_service_state_stack.py infrastructure/tests/unit/test_command_service_worker_stack.py.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Deployment-boundary decision: the command worker is a Plexus dashboard/control-plane service. Deploy it as a Plexus-owned companion CDK stack, independently from the Amplify backend stacks, while binding it to the same authoritative dashboard task API and environment. Do not place its Fargate service, lifecycle resources, queues, or monitoring inside Amplify stacks: the dashboard data stack is close to the CloudFormation resource limit, and the worker has an independent lifecycle and rollout cadence. Client integration repositories deploy their client-specific scoring/API workloads, not this dashboard command worker. Kubernetes will bind the same portable runtime/contract to its own control-plane environment.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Beginning companion-stack composition. First slice will inventory the existing reusable worker/state stacks and infrastructure entry points, then define explicit dashboard-control-plane bindings and synth coverage before any environment deployment wiring.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Inventory result: reusable CommandServiceStateStack and CommandServiceWorkerStack are implemented, but no portable command-worker Dockerfile/image artifact or companion image pipeline exists. The only legacy CommandWorkerStack is EC2/SSM with consumer-specific filesystem defaults and must remain untouched. Next implementation slice is plx-<new child>: package the portable worker container artifact, then compose a Plexus-owned companion stack with explicit dashboard control-plane bindings.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Paused further implementation after identifying that deployment ownership must be grounded in an inventory of deployed production resources, not repository structure. Performing read-only AWS inventory before deciding whether any existing infrastructure entrypoint or stack is appropriate. PR #554 must not be merged/deployed until this review is complete.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text:
## Current acceptance gate

The reusable state and worker constructs remain valid. Composition is incomplete until the dashboard bridge, buildable image, dedicated companion deployment entrypoint, and end-to-end proof all pass together. The companion deployment must use a focused entrypoint and must not be added to the existing mixed infrastructure/app.py.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Staging deployment blocker: the ECS command worker repeatedly exits during Celery prefork startup with OSError 28 while creating /tmp/pymp-*; the task definition is using Fargate default ephemeral storage. Implementing a narrow explicit ephemeral-storage allocation with synthesized-template coverage, then will validate and open the existing feature branch PR to staging.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Validated the staging unblocker: the command-worker Fargate task now explicitly requests 50 GiB ephemeral storage, and the synthesized ECS task-definition assertion passes (`npm test -- --runInBand amplify/command-service/resource.test.ts`: 20 passed). The worker-image dependency-size remediation remains separate follow-up work.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Opened staging PR #562 for the command-service deployment and explicit worker ephemeral-storage fix. Focused CDK resource test passed (20 tests). The ECS circuit-breaker startup blocker is addressed in the PR; dependency/image-size reduction remains a separate follow-up.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Follow-up staging evidence after the 50 GiB fix: ECS revision 3 reaches Celery ready state, then exits in Kombu SQS async polling because pycurl is absent (`ImportError: The curl client requires the pycurl library.`). Implementing a narrow command-worker runtime dependency and regression check.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Implemented and pushed the Kombu SQS runtime correction in PR #562: command-service-runtime now includes pycurl. Added a clean temporary-environment audit that installs only the runtime extra and constructs Kombu CurlClient, plus a supported-Python guard. Validation passed: focused dependency tests (4 passed), clean runtime audit, and Poetry lock consistency check.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Staging feedback-evaluation submission failed before queue dispatch: submitCommand sends commandPayload as an object to an AppSync AWSJSON Task field. Implementing the narrow serialization correction with resolver-level regression coverage; it will be delivered through a new feature-branch PR to staging.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Opened staging PR #564 for the AppSync AWSJSON submission fix. The resolver now serializes commandPayload at the CreateTask boundary; focused submitCommand validation passed (29 tests). Awaiting staging deployment and an end-to-end feedback-evaluation submission proof.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Staging submission reached the next AppSync contract error: submitCommand sends DynamoDB-only `attributeExists` inside ModelTaskConditionInput. The deployed GraphQL input accepts comparison operators (as used by cancelCommand), so the idempotency create condition will be corrected to an allowed non-equality check and covered by the resolver request-shape test.
